body: The change in this test case is technically a breaking change, but the previous behavior was wrong. If user calls `init` twice, the second `init` shouldn't override the previous usertoken with anonymous usertoken (ref: https://github.com/algolia/search-insights.js/pull/251)
The library is not released, so we have this temporary for now. We shouldn't merge this PR yet.

body: The updated `search-insights` now exports these functions, which enables our tests.
is createInsightsClient not enough for this test? it allows a custom requester to be set which here can be a fake one
You're right. We could use a custom requester here. Do you think we should copy&paste `getFunctionalInterface` and `processQueue` in InstantSearch.js instead?
good question, is there no way to cause those methods to be called from the outside somehow?

I don't see any way. They're [used internally](https://github.com/algolia/search-insights.js/blob/chore/wip/lib/entry-umd.ts#L6:L14). And normally people won't need `getFunctionalInterface` or `processQueue` unless they have a very specific usecase (which I can't think of). However here, we need them to control the flow in our test cases like

1. the queue is ready
2. test some stuff
3. let's say the library is loaded now. let's process the queue
I wonder if it would be best to manually set a queue similar to the browser script, and after a condition call aa = createInsightsClient() (which then immediately flushes, like in real life)?

We're already doing the queuing part here https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/blob/fix/insights-test/test/mock/createInsightsClient.ts#L23:L29
Then I should just copy&paste `getFunctionalInterface` and `processQueue` over here, since we haven't seen the real usecase where people need access to those functions. Especially their implementations won't likely change in the future, so it looks okay to copy them.

https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/pull/4712/commits/d0e0fe5111682eeeba0d72e23ca130d2149482a8

@Haroenv what do you think? The only thing we need from `search-insights` is now `AlgoliaAnalytics`. I'll update the PR on that side.
possibly, I'm just not fully sure what exactly the needs are here, personally I'd go for using just the things that are already exported

https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/blob/fix/insights-test/src/middlewares/__tests__/createInsightsMiddleware.ts#L157:L159

In the test cases we need to test things that happen before the umd library is loaded, and after loaded. To control its timing, I had to make `libraryLoadedAndProcessQueue` function which is basically calling `processQueue`. Does it make sense? Let me know if you don't understand any part or have different opinion on this.

In the same spirit of now having to rewrite insights logic here, shouldn't we get some of theses fonctions from the lib ? https://github.com/algolia/search-insights.js/blob/6c58e24abdc8cb7cb334b067a743619c28469db4/lib/_processQueue.ts
`processQueue` and `getFunctionalInterface` are private APIs but actually exported (for internal use). I think I would just use them instead of copy pasting them.

This test file imports `createInsightsClient` from `test/mock/createInsightsClient.ts` and it imports it from `node_modules/search-insights`.

Unless we exclude these two files, `tsc` will type-check `search-insights` and fail.
I tried to avoid it without having to exclude the test file here, but

- https://github.com/Microsoft/TypeScript/issues/14293
- https://github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/issues/36017
- https://www.reddit.com/r/typescript/comments/747xz7/suppress_errors_in_node_modules/

> "exclude" only prevents items from being included by "include"; it doesn't prevent them from being included via import statements or <reference>s. If you import levelup, and levelup imports leveldown, then excluding leveldown or node_modules won't have an effect.

couldn't find a way.
